rows.what the ink shows: The letter has a long rising left shoulder, two narrow joined loops and a right downstroke, like the H in the preceding X′ definition. The nearby X has opposing curved arms and a transverse join instead.
A looped left point opens into separate upper-right and lower-right arms. There is no separate lower wavy or horizontal stroke for lesssim.
A short initial i stroke is followed by a low connector, a deep p/l turn and the descending q-shaped turn before the short final e. The same-page impliquerait has the same initial connected turns.
Under the crossing strokes, a curved left parenthesis, central upright t and closing bowed stroke remain distinguishable. The cancellation overlaps the t crossbar.
The right-hand deleted group retains a separate curved opening stroke, a central tall t with a transverse stroke and a right closing hook. Diagonal deletion strokes cross the middle.
The small leading glyph has a bent upper stroke descending to a short rightward foot. It has no second diagonal crossing through its middle as x would.
The radical’s low check and long rising arm survive at the left. The following A-like diagonals are merged with broad cancellation strokes, so the radicand cannot be secured.
Crossing strokes cover the putative A, membership curve and right-hand looped letter. Several upright and curved remnants survive, but their boundaries and a distinct underline are obscured.
The word begins with a long p down-and-up turn, continues through a low connected middle with an i dot, and ends in a tall f with a descending stem. Its upper end touches the deleted note above.
In the rotated margin, a long initial p descender leads into a low joined r/e group; two small rises and a final trailing e stroke complete preuve. There is no extra separately written word.

The first inserted glyph has a broad open cup and a central stem extending above and below its junction. No upper closing stroke is visible, so its form does not securely distinguish the proposed phi variants; it is also psi-shaped.
The second inserted glyph has a shallow upturned bowl crossed by a tall central stem, with no closed oval. Its especially flat cup leaves the phi variants unresolved and permits a psi-shaped reading.
The lower-right index has a separate initial 1 and plus, then a single A between two upright bars. The A’s center is overtraced, but both legs and its surrounding bars remain visible.

An accented capital É is followed by the descending q turn and an open c; the connected continuation has dotted i strokes, crossed t forms and a final accented ending. The long middle connectors compress several letters.
